tagline.en_US: Cloud storage synchronization and FUSE mounts

description.en_US: Official Rclone image adapted as a native Proxmox OCI LXC with persistent configuration, authenticated WebUI and optional FUSE publication for other LXCs.

catalog_ui.author: Rclone
tips: The installer generates WebUI credentials; the user creates and authorizes their own remote.
FUSE publication is optional and requires a privileged LXC plus explicit Proxmox host adaptations.

container_contract.original_compose:
name: rclone
services:
  rclone:
    image: rclone/rclone:latest
    command:
    - gui
    - --no-open-browser
    - --addr=:5572
    - --api-addr=:5573
    - --config=/config/rclone/rclone.conf
    environment:
      XDG_CONFIG_HOME: /config
    ports:
    - 5572:5572
    - 5573:5573
    volumes:
    - rclone-config:/config/rclone
    - /mnt/oci-shared/rclone/data:/data
    devices:
    - /dev/fuse:/dev/fuse
    cap_add:
    - SYS_ADMIN
    security_opt:
    - apparmor:unconfined
    restart: unless-stopped
volumes:
  rclone-config: {}

adaptations.upstream_behavior: The official Rclone Docker deployment receives /dev/fuse and SYS_ADMIN to run rclone mount.
adaptations.native_lxc_behavior: Create a privileged Proxmox OCI LXC with features fuse=1; a minimal wrapper reads persistent RC credentials, waits for host-managed networking and execs the official Rclone binary as PID 1.
adaptations.reason: FUSE is the core function, and the OCI process can start before Proxmox finishes host-managed networking.
adaptations.behavioral_impact: Equivalent mount and RC behavior; credentials remain at the official persistent configuration boundary.
adaptations.validation: Passed on CT138 with gdrive:; official Rclone became PID 1 and the internal fuse.rclone mount survived stop/start.

adaptations.upstream_behavior: Docker can publish a FUSE submount through a bind configured with shared propagation.
adaptations.native_lxc_behavior: A Proxmox hook starts a transient one-shot waiter after post-start. The waiter clones the FUSE tree from the LXC mount namespace with open_tree, creates canonical read/write and recursive read-only views with mount_setattr, and publishes both in the host namespace with move_mount; pre-stop removes them.
adaptations.reason: LXC makes the container mount tree a slave of the host, so rshared alone cannot propagate a container-created mount back to the host.
adaptations.behavioral_impact: Namespace topology only; no Rclone process, remote protocol or application data is moved to the host.
adaptations.validation: Passed on Proxmox VE 9.2.11/kernel 7.0.14-14-pve: canonical read/write publication, recursive read-only publication, clean unpublish, republish, and simultaneous Plex/Jellyfin consumption.

adaptations.upstream_behavior: Consumers bind the published Docker host path with the requested read/write policy.
adaptations.native_lxc_behavior: Read-only consumers receive the shared remotes-ro root first and one exact mpN from that same intrinsically read-only publication per selected remote second.
adaptations.reason: The parent mount carries future mount/unmount propagation while the exact mpN includes an already-published FUSE tree during consumer startup; the host publication itself enforces read-only after Rclone mount replacement.
adaptations.behavioral_impact: Equivalent consumer path with explicit Proxmox storage metadata.
adaptations.validation: Validated with CT131 Plex and CT128 Jellyfin before and after restarting CT138 Rclone; both exposed the remote through the recursive read-only publication.

data_host_path.description: Directorio local para operaciones copy y sync. No contiene la configuracion persistente.

shared_mount_root.description: Host root where the remote mounts appear, to be assigned afterwards to Plex, Jellyfin, qBittorrent or other OCI containers.

remote_name.description: Remote created by the user; it is never included in the template.

shared_mount_root_parent.description: Punto de montaje del host que contiene las publicaciones de lectura/escritura y de solo lectura; el hook lo configura como rshared.

shared_mount_read_only_root.description: Vista FUSE recursivamente de solo lectura para consumidores multimedia como Plex y Jellyfin.

mounts.purpose: Internal target for official rclone mount before host publication.

deployment.restart_note: On some OCI containers, pct reboot left a residual lxc-start monitor behind. The installer prefers pct stop followed by pct start, and checks the new PID.

setup.purpose: Create and authorize the user's own remote through the authenticated WebUI.

mount.purpose: Mount one selected remote, keep the authenticated RC WebUI/API available and publish the FUSE tree for native Proxmox consumers.
mount.wrapper_behavior: Read RC credentials from /config, wait for host-managed networking, then exec the official Rclone binary.
mount.webui_serving: official --rc-web-gui flags on the RC listener
mount.restart_persistence: Proxmox starts the generated mount wrapper on every boot.

publish_remote.consumer_policy: Consumers are never modified unless the user selects them explicitly.

backup_restore.application_consistency: Use stop mode when active copy or sync jobs require a consistent snapshot. OAuth tokens in rclone.conf are included in the managed config volume.

mount-mode-wrapper.content_template:
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

credentials=/config/rclone/webui.credentials
export RCLONE_RC_USER="$(sed -n 's/^username=//p' "$credentials")"
export RCLONE_RC_PASS="$(sed -n 's/^password=//p' "$credentials")"
remote_name="$(printf '%s' '{{remote_name_base64}}' | base64 -d)"
remote_path="$(printf '%s' '{{remote_path_base64}}' | base64 -d)"

test -n "$RCLONE_RC_USER"
test -n "$RCLONE_RC_PASS"
test -n "$remote_name"

network_ready=false
for _ in $(seq 1 120); do
  if ip route get 1.1.1.1 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    network_ready=true
    break
  fi
  sleep 1
done
test "$network_ready" = true

exec /usr/local/bin/rclone mount "${remote_name}:${remote_path}" /data/mounts/{{mount_name}} \
  --config /config/rclone/rclone.conf \
  --allow-other \
  --vfs-cache-mode {{vfs_cache_mode}} \
  --cache-dir /config/rclone/cache \
  --rc \
  --rc-addr :{{webui_port}} \
  --rc-web-gui \
  --rc-web-gui-no-open-browser \
  --log-file /config/rclone/rclone.log \
  --log-level ERROR

mount-tree-publisher-source.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Clone a FUSE mount from an LXC namespace into the Proxmox host namespace."""

from __future__ import annotations

import ctypes
import os
import platform
import sys


AT_FDCWD = -100
AT_EMPTY_PATH = 0x1000
AT_RECURSIVE = 0x8000
CLONE_NEWNS = 0x00020000
MOVE_MOUNT_F_EMPTY_PATH = 0x00000004
MOUNT_ATTR_RDONLY = 0x00000001
OPEN_TREE_CLONE = 1

SYSCALLS = {
    "x86_64": (428, 429, 442),
    "amd64": (428, 429, 442),
    "aarch64": (428, 429, 442),
    "arm64": (428, 429, 442),
}


class MountAttr(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_ = [
        ("attr_set", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("attr_clr", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("propagation", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("userns_fd", ctypes.c_uint64),
    ]


def fail(step: str) -> None:
    error = ctypes.get_errno()
    raise OSError(error, f"{step}: {os.strerror(error)}")


def main() -> int:
    if len(sys.argv) != 5 or sys.argv[4] not in {"rw", "ro"}:
        print(f"usage: {sys.argv[0]} PID SOURCE TARGET rw|ro", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    machine = platform.machine().lower()
    if machine not in SYSCALLS:
        print(f"unsupported host architecture: {machine}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    open_tree_nr, move_mount_nr, mount_setattr_nr = SYSCALLS[machine]
    pid, source, target, mode = sys.argv[1:]
    libc = ctypes.CDLL(None, use_errno=True)
    libc.syscall.restype = ctypes.c_long
    libc.setns.argtypes = (ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int)
    libc.setns.restype = ctypes.c_int

    host_ns = os.open("/proc/self/ns/mnt", os.O_RDONLY | os.O_CLOEXEC)
    host_root = os.open("/", os.O_PATH | os.O_DIRECTORY | os.O_CLOEXEC)
    ct_ns = os.open(f"/proc/{pid}/ns/mnt", os.O_RDONLY | os.O_CLOEXEC)
    ct_root = os.open(f"/proc/{pid}/root", os.O_PATH | os.O_DIRECTORY | os.O_CLOEXEC)
    try:
        if libc.setns(ct_ns, CLONE_NEWNS) != 0:
            fail("enter container namespace")
        os.fchdir(ct_root)
        os.chroot(".")
        os.chdir("/")
        tree = libc.syscall(
            open_tree_nr,
            AT_FDCWD,
            os.fsencode(source),
            OPEN_TREE_CLONE | os.O_CLOEXEC,
        )
        if tree < 0:
            fail("clone source mount tree")
        try:
            if mode == "ro":
                attributes = MountAttr(attr_set=MOUNT_ATTR_RDONLY)
                result = libc.syscall(
                    mount_setattr_nr,
                    tree,
                    ctypes.c_char_p(b""),
                    AT_EMPTY_PATH | AT_RECURSIVE,
                    ctypes.byref(attributes),
                    ctypes.sizeof(attributes),
                )
                if result != 0:
                    fail("make cloned mount tree read-only")
            if libc.setns(host_ns, CLONE_NEWNS) != 0:
                fail("return to host namespace")
            os.fchdir(host_root)
            os.chroot(".")
            os.chdir("/")
            result = libc.syscall(
                move_mount_nr,
                tree,
                ctypes.c_char_p(b""),
                AT_FDCWD,
                os.fsencode(target),
                MOVE_MOUNT_F_EMPTY_PATH,
            )
            if result != 0:
                fail("publish mount tree")
        finally:
            os.close(tree)
    finally:
        for descriptor in (ct_root, ct_ns, host_root, host_ns):
            os.close(descriptor)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        raise SystemExit(main())
    except OSError as exc:
        print(exc, file=sys.stderr)
        raise SystemExit(1)

mount-publication-waiter.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

vmid=${1:?missing VMID}
inside=${2:?missing source path}
published=${3:?missing target path}
published_ro=${4:?missing read-only target path}
helper=${5:?missing publisher helper}

unpublish() {
  local target=$1
  if mountpoint -q "$target"; then
    umount "$target" || umount -l "$target"
  fi
}

for _ in $(seq 1 300); do
  pid=$(lxc-info -n "$vmid" -pH 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [[ -n $pid ]] && awk -v path="$inside" '$5 == path && $0 ~ / - fuse(\.rclone)? / { found=1 } END { exit !found }' "/proc/$pid/mountinfo"; then
    unpublish "$published_ro"
    unpublish "$published"
    "$helper" "$pid" "$inside" "$published" rw
    if ! "$helper" "$pid" "$inside" "$published_ro" ro; then
      unpublish "$published"
      exit 1
    fi
    findmnt -T "$published" -n -o FSTYPE | grep -q '^fuse'
    findmnt -T "$published_ro" -n -o FSTYPE | grep -q '^fuse'
    findmnt -T "$published_ro" -n -o VFS-OPTIONS | tr ',' '
' | grep -qx ro
    logger -t proxmenux-rclone "Published CT $vmid $inside at $published (rw) and $published_ro (ro)"
    exit 0
  fi
  sleep 1
done

logger -t proxmenux-rclone "Timed out waiting for CT $vmid FUSE mount at $inside"
exit 1

consumer_integration.restart_rule: Keep both parent and exact mpN declarations so consumers recover when the Rclone FUSE publication is replaced.

notes: La configuracion, los tokens y las credenciales RC permanecen en /config/rclone dentro del volumen backup=1.
El usuario crea y autoriza su propio remote desde la WebUI; la plantilla no incluye remotes del laboratorio.
El modo mount usa un wrapper minimo que termina con exec del binario oficial; Rclone queda como PID 1.
La publicacion usa un hookscript oficial de Proxmox y una tarea systemd transitoria; no instala Rclone ni un supervisor permanente en el host.
Cada remoto se publica en una raiz canonica de lectura/escritura y en otra raiz recursivamente de solo lectura; cada consumidor selecciona la politica adecuada.
Los consumidores son opcionales y deben declarar el padre compartido mas un mpN exacto por remoto.
El perfil fue validado con reinicios de Rclone, Plex y Jellyfin.

security_profile.warning: Rclone mount requires a privileged LXC with FUSE access. Use this profile only on a trusted node and network.

compatibility.policy: Automatic installation implements the validated privileged FUSE LXC, generated wrappers, and host publication workflow with explicit user consent.
